verdict: A promising project with a real problem behind it, undermined by a likely target-leakage issue and an overclaimed deployment slide. The presenter recovered well under questioning.

criteria.name: Clarity
criteria.comment: Clear story on slides 1-2; slide 6 was unreadable and ran long.

criteria.name: Rigour and evidence
criteria.comment: Headline claim lacked a baseline until challenged; possible target leakage not checked; LightGBM attribution wrong.

criteria.name: Handling questions
criteria.comment: Answered directly, admitted the leakage gap honestly, explained rolling-origin validation.

criteria.name: Time management
criteria.comment: Ignored the first two-minute reminder; needed an escalation before moving on.

moments.quote: our model is forty percent better
moments.note: Comparative claim with no baseline or metric until challenged.

moments.quote: the baseline is the hospital's current rolling average, and the metric is mean absolute error

moments.note: Factual error, corrected by fact-check: LightGBM is Microsoft's (around 2016).

moments.quote: and the next group is holiday features
moments.note: Kept talking through the two-minute reminder; escalation needed.

moments.quote: kami belum cek apakah waktu ke dokter itu masuk ke target, tapi kami bisa retrain tanpa fitur itu
moments.note: Honest about the leakage gap and proposed a concrete fix (answered in Indonesian).

improvements: Remove or justify 'time to first physician': confirm it is available at prediction time.
State the baseline and metric on the headline slide itself.
Cut slide 6 to the three most important features, with evidence of their importance.
